messages:
maya: heads up — the recompute run kicked off at 04:30 UTC and we saw a big spike in quota/ingest tokens. some internal APIs started hitting per-project throttles and a couple of customer requests were delayed. not sure if batch routing bumped to hosted tier or stayed on shared GPUs.

zach: saw it too. job id recompute-agg-2025-04-30-01. lots of small shards but high fanout, so requests overlapped.

sasha: hmm sounds like we lack a backfill-specific routing label. do we tag these runs so router can prefer dedicated/delayed lanes?

maya: currently airflow triggers with header X-Redwood-Backfill=true in the job metadata, but router ignores it. routing policies only look at model + customer tier + region.

ara: proposal: add a "workload_class" enum (realtime, standard, backfill_low, backfill_high). router can map backfill_high -> dedicated_or_fallback, backfill_low -> spot/batch pool. low impact to latency.

leo: agree. also need quota accounting separation. right now backfills consume same per-project token quota which means orgs doing large recomputes can eat their realtime allowance. we should add a separate quota bucket for backfill runs that can be throttled independently.

zach: +1. Implementation question: do we surface backfill quotas in console? ops folks want visibility and the ability to burn a reserved backfill allotment.

maya: yes — console should show: allocated backfill token budget, used, ETA for completion, and ability to pause/resume. ideally estimate token burn before starting.

ara: on the router side, we also need a simple circuit-breaker: if shared GPU pool CPU or token rate > 80% for 5m, divert backfill_high automatically. avoids cascading throttle.

infra-bot: deploybot: rolling deploy of router-v2 scheduled for 05:15 UTC — will include workload_class header parsing and priority mapping.

sasha: regarding metrics: we need a distinct telemetry tag so we can segregate metrics in sums/percentiles. add label "recompute=true" and "backfill_class=high|low" to every emitted event during the run. that will help backfill dashboards.

leo: for safety, we should do a dry-run/estimate mode in the kick-off CLI — something like:

```
airflow trigger_dag recompute_agg --conf '{"shard":1024, "estimate_only": true, "workload_class": "backfill_high"}'
```

and return an estimated token count and projected wall time. ops can approve to proceed.

maya: +1. small UX ask: add a one-click "estimate & schedule" in the console where you can pick windows, soft-throttle %, and preferred pool (dedicated/spot).

zach: one tricky bit: model routing. some older quantized variants are cheaper but slower; backfills can tolerate that. so router should consider model_variant_preference when workload_class != realtime. e.g., prefer quant-4bit variants for backfill_low.

ara: note: we must ensure KV-cache semantics don't break recompute correctness when switching variants. add a validation step in the job planner.

sasha: also need audit logs for customer-facing queries delayed by backfills; product wants a list of affected request ids if SLA border gets touched. put a sampling flag by default.

leo: for quotas: suggested policy = per-org realtime_quota + backfill_quota (monthly allotment) + overage_rate. backfill can be rate-limited to X tokens/min with exponential backoff.

maya: operational checklist for router-v2 rollout:
- enable workload_class header parsing (feature flag)
- route backfill_high to dedicated pool if capacity >= threshold
- add backfill quota type in billing/quotas service
- emit telemetry labels for all backfill runs
- add console estimate UI (opt-in)

zach: can we pilot with a single internal org first? use low-risk datasets and a small backfill_quota. then ramp.

ara: yes. I'll add a canary toggle in planner. also add a safeguard: if any realtime SLO breach > 2% during pilot, auto-pause backfills.

sasha: who owns the console bits? devex? pinging @leo for product/UX tradeoffs.

leo: devex + product can do a light MVP — estimate modal + schedule + budget slider. I'll draft a mock tomorrow.

maya: for now let's document the API changes: header name X-Redwood-Workload-Class values = realtime|standard|backfill_low|backfill_high; telemetry labels recompute=true, backfill_class=...; quota key backfill_tokens:{org_id}:{month}.

zach: quick NOTE: batch job logs show a bunch of 429s from auth-service around 04:38 — might need token bucket adjustments for job actors.

ara: good catch. add a small retry jitter and lower concurrent client connections in the recompute workers until router-v2 lands.

infra-bot: alertbot: created incident INC-2050 for auth-service 429 spike (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2050).

maya: next steps: ara + zach implement router side changes + circuit-breaker; leo + devex mock console; sasha add telemetry labels and backfill quota storage; i'll coordinate pilot schedule.

leo: ETA for router change PR? a day or two?

ara: I'll aim for a PR today, bench tests tomorrow.

zach: I'll add quota schema + billing hook. maybe need help from finance to define overage rate. cc @finance later.

maya: thanks all. let's keep this thread for quick synces. if anything urgent ping me in #eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
